slides.title: Example flows
slides.subtitle: Follow each PAP feature from a user's intent to a safe agent result
slides.notes: These pages walk through the protocol behaviour that the runnable Python and Agent Runtimes examples demonstrate. Each one takes a single feature and follows it from what the user wants to what the agent can safely say about it.

slides.title: What every flow shows
slides.diagram:
flowchart LR M["Model"] subgraph HOST["Host code and Reactor contributions"] direction TB T["PAP client"] --- K["Keys, tokens,
browser, state"] end CO["Company"] HOST -- "assertions, Session JWTs, tokens" --> CO CO -- "verified answers" --> HOST HOST -. "status, scopes, booleans" .-> M
slides.caption: Where the data travels, who owns the sensitive work, and what may reach the model.
slides.notes: Every page answers the same three questions. Which requests go where; which Reactor capability holds the keys, tokens and secrets; and what is left that the model may see. The answer to the last one is always: much less than the host knows. In the picture: the secrets cross only between the host and the company; the model, on the dotted line, gets a safe summary.

slides.title: Before a Session

items.title: Company discovery
items.detail: Resolve and validate public PAP capabilities

items.title: Agent identity
items.detail: Verify agent metadata and signing policy

items.title: Delegation
items.detail: Vouch for a delegated key, naming no User and no Company

items.title: Session JWT
items.detail: Bind one Session JWT to one HTTP request

slides.notes: The first flows are the building blocks. A personal agent finds out what a company supports, the company checks who the agent is, and the agent learns to make the two signed things every request depends on: a delegation that vouches for a delegated key, and a Session JWT signed with that key.

slides.caption: Every flow happens in a Session; sign-in and refresh tokens unlock what needs the account.
slides.notes: The middle of the set builds on those blocks. Sessions start and travel safely; users sign in without the model ever touching OAuth state or tokens; and conversations carry messages, events, streams and the operations a user approves.

slides.title: Two journeys put it together

left.heading: A user with a company
left.content: Ada asks Atlas to exchange a jacket at **Manzanita**: discovery to sign-out, both sides from the SDK.

right.heading: Two companies
right.content: **Ledgerly** pays Ada's invoices at **Northwind Bank**, by composing two PAP relationships.

slides.notes: Each other page showcases one feature. The last two combine several: one user with one company from first question to sign-out, and an accounting firm acting for the same user at her bank.

slides.title: Runnable without real credentials
items: Deterministic or local transports where needed
Newer flows use the reference company in `personal_agent_protocol.demo`
Real keys and real HTTP over ASGI, in one process, no network
Production hosts swap the fixtures through **Reactor contributions**
slides.notes: The examples teach the boundary without any real secret. The newer ones talk to a reference company with real keys and real HTTP, all inside one process. In production, the same code gets egress, state, browsers, signing, delegated key custody and token storage from Reactor contributions.

slides.title: Two implementations, one boundary
slides.notes: Every flow exists twice. The PAP repository has plain Pydantic AI examples, and Agent Runtimes has matching Loop applications with interactive Reactor views. The protocol and the rules for handling secrets are identical in both.

slides.title: Shown by an example alone
items: **Company APIs**: OpenAPI with the Session header; MCP with an access token for its URL alone
**Sign-in display**: what a page and a model each get of `PapSignIn`
**Telemetry**: one allowlisted event per protocol stage
slides.notes: A few features have a runnable Pydantic AI example and a guide, but no page of their own here. They cover calling a company's APIs, building a company, displaying a sign-in, and telemetry.
